notes.definition: Protist diseases are communicable diseases caused by protists, which are single-celled organisms. The example you need is malaria, caused by a protist whose life cycle includes the mosquito.
explanation: Protists are one of the four types of pathogen. They are single-celled organisms, larger and more complex than bacteria, with a nucleus. The pathogens that cause malaria are protists. Malaria is one of the most important infectious diseases in the world, especially in hot countries where mosquitoes are common.

The malarial protist has a life cycle that includes the mosquito. When a mosquito feeds on the blood of an infected person, it takes in protists. The protists develop inside the mosquito. When the mosquito then bites another person, it passes the protists into that person's blood, where they reproduce. The mosquito is a vector: an organism that carries the pathogen from one host to another. Malaria cannot pass directly from person to person by touching or coughing.

Malaria causes recurrent episodes of fever. This means the fever comes back again and again, every few days, as the protists reproduce and are released into the blood. Malaria can be fatal, particularly in young children. People who survive may become ill again and again.

The spread of malaria is controlled by stopping the vector. One way is preventing mosquitoes from breeding. Mosquitoes lay their eggs in still water, where the larvae develop, so draining areas of standing water or spraying breeding sites with insecticide reduces the number of mosquitoes. Another way is using mosquito nets to avoid being bitten, especially at night when the mosquitoes feed. Nets treated with insecticide also kill mosquitoes that land on them. Fewer bites means fewer protists are passed between people.
keyFacts: The pathogens that cause malaria are protists.
The malarial protist has a life cycle that includes the mosquito.
The mosquito is the vector of malaria.
Malaria causes recurrent episodes of fever.
Spread is controlled by preventing mosquitoes (the vectors) from breeding.
Mosquito nets are used to avoid being bitten.

keyTerms.definition: A single-celled organism with a nucleus; some protists are pathogens, such as the one that causes malaria.
A disease caused by a protist, spread by mosquitoes, causing recurrent episodes of fever; it can be fatal.
An organism that carries a pathogen from one host to another; the mosquito is the vector for malaria.
The stages an organism passes through; the malarial protist's life cycle includes both humans and mosquitoes.
Happening again and again; malaria fevers keep returning.
A fine mesh net, often placed over beds, that stops mosquitoes biting people.

workedExamples.title: Explaining vector control
workedExamples.question: Explain why draining ponds and ditches near a village reduces the number of cases of malaria.
steps: Mosquitoes lay their eggs in still water, where the larvae develop.
Draining the water removes breeding sites, so fewer mosquitoes are produced.
Mosquitoes are the vectors that carry the malarial protist between people.
Fewer mosquitoes means fewer people are bitten and infected.
workedExamples.answer: It stops mosquitoes breeding, so there are fewer vectors to carry the protist to people.

workedExamples.title: Analysing net data
workedExamples.question: In a study, 48 out of 1200 children who slept under mosquito nets caught malaria, compared with 156 out of 1200 who did not. Calculate the percentage of each group that caught malaria and comment on the result.
steps: The percentage without nets is more than three times higher (13 ÷ 4 = 3.25).
Nets reduce bites, so fewer protists are passed on.
workedExamples.answer: 4% with nets and 13% without; nets greatly reduce the chance of catching malaria.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think malaria is caused by mosquitoes.
misconceptions.right: In fact malaria is caused by a protist. The mosquito is only the vector that carries it.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think malaria is caused by a virus or bacterium.
misconceptions.right: In fact the pathogen is a protist, a single-celled organism with a nucleus.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think malaria can be caught from an infected person's coughs or by touching them.
misconceptions.right: In fact malaria is passed between people by mosquito bites, as the protist's life cycle includes the mosquito.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think malaria causes one fever which then goes away.
misconceptions.right: In fact malaria causes recurrent episodes of fever that keep returning.

realWorld: Charities distribute insecticide-treated bed nets in parts of Africa and Asia, which has prevented many deaths from malaria.
Draining swamps and standing water helped to remove malaria from parts of southern Europe and the USA in the twentieth century.
Travellers to countries where malaria is common use insect repellent, cover up in the evening and sleep under nets.
Health workers spray insecticide in homes and on breeding sites to reduce mosquito numbers.
examTips: Always state that malaria is caused by a protist and that the mosquito is the vector. Saying 'mosquitoes cause malaria' loses marks.
Use the phrase 'recurrent episodes of fever' for the symptom.
For control, link each method to the vector: preventing breeding reduces mosquito numbers; nets stop people being bitten.
In data questions on nets or insecticides, compare percentages rather than raw numbers when group sizes differ.
summary: Malaria is caused by a protist (a single-celled organism).
The malarial protist's life cycle includes the mosquito, which is the vector.
Malaria causes recurrent episodes of fever and can be fatal.
Spread is controlled by preventing mosquitoes from breeding.
Mosquito nets help people avoid being bitten.

questions.question: What type of pathogen causes malaria?
markScheme: 1 mark: protist
questions.explanation: The pathogens that cause malaria are protists. The mosquito is the vector, not the pathogen.

questions.question: Which organism is the vector for malaria?
markScheme: 1 mark: mosquito
questions.explanation: The malarial protist has a life cycle that includes the mosquito, which carries it between people.

questions.question: What is the main symptom of malaria?
markScheme: 1 mark: recurrent episodes of fever
questions.explanation: Malaria causes recurrent episodes of fever and can be fatal. A rash is measles; diarrhoea is Salmonella.

questions.question: Which of these helps people avoid being bitten by mosquitoes at night?
markScheme: 1 mark: mosquito nets
questions.explanation: Mosquito nets physically stop mosquitoes reaching sleeping people. Antibiotics do not kill protists, fungicides kill fungi and the measles vaccine does not protect against malaria.

questions.question: Why does preventing mosquitoes from breeding reduce the spread of malaria?
options: It kills the protists in infected people
There are fewer vectors to carry the protist between people
It makes people immune to malaria
markScheme: 1 mark: fewer vectors to carry the protist
questions.explanation: Fewer mosquitoes means fewer bites, so fewer protists are carried from infected to healthy people. It does not affect protists already inside a person.

questions.question: Mosquitoes lay their eggs in still water. Which action would most directly prevent mosquitoes breeding?
markScheme: 1 mark: draining areas of standing water
questions.explanation: Removing still water removes the breeding sites. Long sleeves reduce bites but do not prevent breeding.

questions.question: Which statement about the malarial protist is correct?
options: It can only live in water
It is spread by droplets from coughs
It has a life cycle that includes the mosquito
It is a type of fungus
markScheme: 1 mark: it has a life cycle that includes the mosquito
questions.explanation: The specification states that the malarial protist has a life cycle that includes the mosquito. It is a protist, not a fungus, and is not spread by droplets.

questions.question: In a village, the number of mosquitoes falls sharply after an insecticide spraying programme, but malaria cases do not fall for several weeks. Which is the best explanation?
options: Insecticides increase the number of protists
People who were already infected still have protists in their blood and continue to have symptoms
Malaria is spread directly from person to person
markScheme: 1 mark: people already infected still have protists in their blood
questions.explanation: Killing mosquitoes prevents new infections, but people already infected still carry the protists and remain ill, so recorded cases fall only after a delay.

questions.question: Malaria is not found in the UK today, even though infected travellers sometimes arrive. Which is the most likely reason it does not spread here?
options: Few mosquitoes here can act as vectors, as the cool climate stops the protist developing inside them
The protist cannot survive in human blood in the UK
Everyone in the UK is vaccinated against malaria
Malaria is only spread by drinking water
markScheme: 1 mark: there are few suitable mosquito vectors to pass on the protist
questions.explanation: Malaria needs the mosquito vector to pass from person to person, and the protist must develop inside the mosquito, which needs warm conditions. Without effective vectors, an infected traveller cannot pass it on. It is not spread by water and there is no routine UK vaccination.

questions.question: Why are insecticide-treated nets more effective than untreated nets?
options: They kill the protists in the person's blood
They also kill mosquitoes that land on them, reducing the number of vectors
They release a vaccine into the air
They stop mosquitoes laying eggs in water
markScheme: 1 mark: they also kill mosquitoes, reducing vectors
questions.explanation: Treated nets stop bites and kill mosquitoes that land on them, so there are fewer vectors overall.

questions.question: In a study, 1200 children slept under mosquito nets. 48 of them caught malaria. Calculate the percentage of these children who caught malaria.
In the same study, 156 out of 1200 children who did not use nets caught malaria, compared with 48 out of 1200 who did. How many times more likely were children without nets to catch malaria?
questions.explanation: The group sizes are equal, so divide 156 by 48 = 3.25. Children without nets were 3.25 times as likely to catch malaria.

questions.question: The number of malaria cases in a region fell from 2.4 million to 1.8 million per year. Calculate the percentage decrease.
markScheme: 1 mark: 2.4 − 1.8 = 0.6 million
questions.explanation: Decrease ÷ original × 100 = 0.6 ÷ 2.4 × 100 = 25%.

questions.question: Before ponds near a village were drained, scientists counted 840 mosquito larvae in water samples. After draining, they counted 126 larvae in the same number of samples. Calculate the percentage reduction in larvae.
questions.explanation: 714 ÷ 840 × 100 = 85%. Using 126 as the denominator would be wrong because the original value was 840.

questions.question: Name the type of pathogen that causes malaria.
markScheme: 1 mark: protist
questions.explanation: Malaria is caused by a protist.

questions.question: Give two ways the spread of malaria can be controlled.
markScheme: 1 mark: preventing mosquitoes from breeding (e.g. draining still water, insecticide on breeding sites)
1 mark: using mosquito nets to avoid being bitten
questions.explanation: Both methods target the vector, which is how the specification says malaria spread is controlled.

questions.question: Explain what is meant by the statement 'the mosquito is a vector for malaria'.
acceptedAnswers: does not cause the disease itself
markScheme: 1 mark: the mosquito carries the pathogen (protist)
1 mark: from one person (host) to another
questions.explanation: A vector carries a pathogen between hosts; it is not the pathogen itself.

questions.question: Describe the symptoms of malaria.
markScheme: 1 mark: recurrent episodes of fever
1 mark: can be fatal
questions.explanation: The specification describes malaria as causing recurrent episodes of fever and states it can be fatal.

questions.question: Explain why sleeping under a mosquito net reduces a person's risk of malaria.
markScheme: 1 mark: the net stops mosquitoes biting the person (at night when they feed)
1 mark: so the protist is not passed into their blood
questions.explanation: The protist enters the blood through a mosquito bite, so preventing bites prevents infection.

questions.question: Describe how the malarial protist is passed from an infected person to a healthy person.
markScheme: 1 mark: a mosquito bites an infected person and takes in protists with the blood
1 mark: the protists develop inside the mosquito
1 mark: the mosquito bites a healthy person and passes the protists into their blood
questions.explanation: The protist's life cycle includes the mosquito, so transmission always goes human, mosquito, human.

questions.question: Suggest why malaria cannot be controlled by isolating infected people in the same way as measles.
markScheme: 1 mark: malaria is not spread directly between people (or by droplets); it is spread by mosquitoes
1 mark: mosquitoes could still bite the isolated person and carry protists to others, so controlling the vector is more effective
questions.explanation: Isolation works for diseases spread by contact or droplets. Malaria needs a vector, so stopping the vector is the key.

questions.question: State why it is important to control malaria.
markScheme: 1 mark: malaria can be fatal
questions.explanation: Malaria can kill, so preventing its spread saves lives.

questions.question: Describe the cause and symptoms of malaria and explain how mosquito nets help to control it.
markScheme: Indicative content: caused by a protist; protist's life cycle includes the mosquito; mosquito is the vector; recurrent episodes of fever; can be fatal; nets stop mosquitoes biting people (especially at night); so protists not passed into blood; insecticide-treated nets also kill mosquitoes.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): correct cause and symptoms plus a clear explanation of how nets work.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): some correct points about cause, symptoms or nets.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: Cover all three parts: cause (protist, mosquito vector), symptoms (recurrent fever, can be fatal) and control (nets prevent bites).

questions.question:
A charity has funding to reduce malaria in a region with many swamps and ponds. It could spend the money on draining breeding sites or on giving every family insecticide-treated mosquito nets.
Explain how each method reduces the spread of malaria, and evaluate which would be the better use of the money.
markScheme: Indicative content: malaria caused by a protist; mosquito is the vector; life cycle includes mosquito. Draining: removes still water where mosquitoes breed, so fewer mosquitoes and fewer bites; benefits everyone in the area; but expensive, large swamps hard to drain, may damage habitats, mosquitoes may breed in other water. Nets: stop people being bitten at night; treated nets also kill mosquitoes; cheaper per person and quick to distribute; but only work if used correctly and do not protect during the day or outdoors; nets may tear. Judgement supported by reasoning, e.g. nets give quicker, cheaper protection, while draining gives a longer-term reduction; a combination may be best.
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): clear explanation of how both methods reduce spread, linked to the vector, with balanced evaluation and a justified conclusion.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): explains both methods with some advantages or disadvantages; conclusion may be missing or unsupported.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple statements about one or both methods.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: Both methods target the vector. A strong answer weighs cost, speed, effectiveness and environmental impact before reaching a supported judgement.

questions.question: Compare how malaria and measles are spread and how the spread of each is controlled.
markScheme: Indicative content: malaria caused by a protist, measles by a virus; malaria spread by mosquito (vector) bites; measles spread by inhalation of droplets from coughs and sneezes; malaria controlled by preventing mosquitoes breeding and mosquito nets; measles controlled mainly by vaccinating young children (and isolation, covering coughs).
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): clear comparison of both route and control for both diseases.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): some correct points for one or both diseases.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: Different routes need different control: vector control for malaria, vaccination for measles.

questions.question: Which statement describes a protist?
options: A non-living particle that reproduces only inside cells
A single-celled organism with a nucleus
markScheme: 1 mark: a single-celled organism with a nucleus
questions.explanation: Protists are single-celled and have a nucleus. A particle that only reproduces in cells describes a virus; a cell with no nucleus describes a bacterium.

questions.question: Suggest why malaria is most common in hot, wet countries.
markScheme: 1 mark: there is more standing water/warm conditions where mosquitoes breed
1 mark: so there are more mosquitoes (vectors) to carry the protist
questions.explanation: The disease depends on its vector. Warm, wet conditions provide breeding sites, so mosquito numbers are high.
